title: The Fourth Night: Where the Center of the World Is
coreMove: Replace the wish to be central or above with one visible act of horizontal contribution.
sourcePressure: The source supports this chapter as relationship reconstruction after task separation: relationships aim toward connection and contribution, the self is not the center of the world, rebuke and praise can preserve vertical posture, value is felt through contribution, and someone has to begin.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says be humble and kind; the real move changes the posture of relationship from evaluator and evaluated to people contributing beside each other.

sourceAnchors.name: Do Not Rebuke or Praise
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source lists this as a visible fourth-night heading and the sidecar notes that both can reinforce vertical relationship structure.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Rebuke and praise can wear opposite faces while keeping the same ladder in the room.

sourceAnchors.name: Someone Has to Start
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source lists this as a visible fourth-night heading and the sidecar says one person must begin the healthier relational shift.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A horizontal room rarely appears by consensus; someone has to stop climbing first.

hook: You are not the center of the universe
Real value comes from helping others
counterintuition: Contribution is the real source of worth

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.audience: a field-team coordinator who usually corrects from above after a missed sweep pattern
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next search may depend on whether tired volunteers can learn without being put below the coordinator
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sarah puts the map on the hood, kneels beside the volunteers, and asks where the pattern broke instead of rebuking them from the tailgate.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Rain beads on a laminated grid map spread across the hood of a mud-streaked truck.

exampleSpecs.audience: a sous-chef who uses praise and scolding to keep trainees dependent on his approval
exampleSpecs.stakes: a Saturday service may fail if the new garde-manger cook keeps waiting for evaluation instead of joining the work
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Marco stops saying 'perfect' and instead works beside the trainee to reset the station standard as shared contribution to service.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Don't look at me after every plate," Marco says, sliding the squeeze bottle back into the rail.

exampleSpecs.audience: a teaching assistant who realizes her detailed praise keeps students writing for her approval
exampleSpecs.stakes: the seminar may become a performance for grades instead of a room where students think with each other
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It takes Anya two essay cycles to replace approval labels with questions that put her beside the student in the problem.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Anya two stacks of blue-book essays to notice how often every margin note crowned or corrected.

exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator who wants to prove he is the indispensable center whenever borrowers clash
exampleSpecs.stakes: a shared tool library may become one person's kingdom instead of a community practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Daniel leaves the broken tile saw on the folding table and asks the two borrowers to design the check-out repair rule with him, not through him.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The tile saw smells of wet cement and scorched dust.
mustAvoid: tools as repeated physical anchor later

exampleSpecs.audience: a principal violinist who confuses leadership with approving and correcting the second stand
exampleSpecs.stakes: the orchestra's entrance keeps fraying because younger players are watching her face instead of the conductor
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Juliette lower her bow during rehearsal and count the entrance with the section instead of giving a pleased nod after they follow her.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see every second violin glance sideways before the downbeat.

exampleSpecs.audience: a maintainer who keeps reviews vertical by approving, rejecting, and rescuing every patch
exampleSpecs.stakes: a useful project may die when the maintainer burns out as the permanent center
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lin turns one pull request into a shared maintainer checklist and lets a newer contributor merge after the checks pass.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What if the merge button is not proof that you are still necessary?

skillTargets: identify vertical posture inside both rebuke and praise
choose horizontal contribution without making the self central
distinguish value through participation from approval capture
evaluate when someone is using help to remain above others

tryThisNowSpec: In one relationship today, replace an approving or correcting sentence with a beside-you question about the shared task.
